core_principles: Brace the core to maintain a neutral spine.
Lower the body with control until the chest approaches the floor.
Place the hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
Press back to the starting position while maintaining alignment.
Maintain a straight line from the head to the heels.
Establish a strong plank position before beginning the movement.
Use incline push-ups for beginner clients to develop strength and movement competency before progressing to standard variations.
Maintain proper alignment to target intended muscles, ensure efficient movement patterns, and reduce discomfort from poor mechanics.
Adjust push-up difficulty by modifying body position, leverage, stability demands, or training volume.
Utilize the push-up as a movement assessment to evaluate upper-body strength, core stability, and the ability to maintain alignment under load.
Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and feet together or hip-width apart.
Engage the core by drawing the navel toward the spine, maintaining a straight line from head to heels.
Lower the body by bending the elbows until the chest nearly touches the floor, keeping elbows at approximately 45 degrees from the body.
Press upward by extending the elbows, avoiding locking them out at the top to maintain continuous tension.
Descend until the chest nearly touches the floor or elbows bend to approximately 90 degrees, avoiding excessive depth or bouncing.
common_mistakes: Not achieving adequate range of motion
Bouncing at the bottom of the movement
specific_findings: Keep your elbows at approximately 45 degrees from your body.
Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor or your elbows bend to approximately 90 degrees, whichever comes first based on mobility.

core_principles: Maintain alignment of the kinetic chain checkpoints (ears, shoulders, hips, knees, and ankles) in a straight line during both the descent and ascent of the push-up.
Engage deep core stabilizers to prevent the lower back from arching or sagging.
Regress the movement to an elevated surface (such as a counter or wall) if postural integrity cannot be maintained on the floor.
Limit the range of motion to a depth that can be performed pain-free and without compensation.
common_mistakes: Arching or sagging of the lower back (loss of core engagement).
Migration of kinetic chain checkpoints (ears, shoulders, hips, knees, ankles) out of alignment due to fatigue.

core_principles: Regress the push-up by placing hands on a bench or knees on the floor to maintain movement integrity and posture.
Progress the push-up by elevating the feet to increase the challenge.
Maintain optimal body alignment and kinetic chain checkpoints (such as keeping the ears, shoulders, and low back aligned).
Control the speed of movement to avoid using momentum, which increases time under tension and stabilizer recruitment.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or body swaying to complete a movement.
Allowing the shoulders to protract, head to move forward, or low back to arch due to excessive progression height or intensity.
specific_findings: Push-up progression: Elevate feet onto 6 inch box
Lunge progression: start at half stride length, progress to ¾ stride length, and then to full stride length if control is maintained
